items.title: Booking.com Looks to Compete in India With Its Own Payments System and Business Travel
items.summary: Booking.com wants more of India’s travel wallet, not just its hotel bookings. Payments and business travel could help it get there, but local platforms will make that a harder sell.

items.title: United Airlines Cuts Profit Outlook as Jet Fuel Costs Rise
items.summary: Despite the higher fuel costs, United is still seeing high travel demand — premium and loyalty revenues were both up 17%.

items.title: Sonesta Cuts Jobs as a $2 Billion Bid Puts Many of Its Best Hotels in Play
items.summary: Service Properties Trust hired Sonesta to operate 68 of the hotels it owns. But an unsolicited offer for those hotels has created uncertainty. Meanwhile, Sonesta has cut corporate staff.

items.title: Skift Transatlantic Summit 2026: Identifying Growth in a Durable but Fragmenting Corridor
items.summary: The transatlantic corridor is seeing durable demand, and companies will have opportunities to gain a competitive advantage by deftly adapting to competing shifts simultaneously.

items.title: What Boston and Iceland Learned From a Sold-Out Summer of Live Tourism
items.summary: When mega-events land in peak season, success comes not in higher volume, but in earned media and positive sentiment.

items.title: The Hotel Industry Has A Water Problem
items.summary: Summer heat and drought brought hospitality’s use of water into sharp focus. The industry is betting on simple fixes like aerated showerheads and less laundry — the question is whether more structural but costly measures can scale.

items.title: AI Will Know Your Travelers. And the World’s Travelers. Will You?
items.summary: AI discovery is moving closer to transaction. Travel brands must become legible to machines without surrendering the memory, service, and loyalty advantages that set them apart.
